note: Session corrections applied: (1) the former 'C4' Atacama-region-wide drilling claim is removed; Stoker et al. 2023 (S08) supports only the ARADS feature (C6), never the Atacama region or Yungay. (2) claim_evidence_class now follows the supporting source's access level only: A requires a full_text_checked AND peer-reviewed supporting source; B allows abstract_only/partial_full_text, or a program_page/data_release supporting source; C is indirect/contextual and must stay 'draft'. Class is never assigned A from an abstract alone. (3) Hardening pass F-06: 'full_text_checked' means the complete source was read, not merely most of it. S06 and S08 were each read to only ~75-80% and are now 'partial_full_text', so C6 (previously the only class-A claim) is now class B. It is intentional and acceptable that this curated dataset currently contains ZERO class-A claims -- none has had its single supporting source read to completion. Every claim also carries an explicit reference_body (mars for all eight, since every Phase 2 research task is Mars-focused), enforced in the database regardless of whether reference_region_code is set. All claims below remain 'draft' pending the open verification gates (section 17 of the spec) and the owner's full-text reading (gate V-10). Project Scope additions: C10 (Gilf Kebir x Jezero, GPR), C11 (Western Desert x Bagnold Dunes, aeolian), C12 (Dakhla x Jezero, fluvial) -- all project_decision_provisional, class B, draft. C3 moved from C to B because S02's abstract is now verified (Crossref). Owner decision 2026-11-12: all eleven claims (class B) are published for the NASA Space Apps demo; their limitations and open verification gates still apply and are shown with every claim.

claims.differences: Not stated in abstract_only reading of S01; to be completed from full text.
claims.not_supported: This record does not support treating Earth weather, atmospheric pressure, radiation, gravity or atmospheric composition as equivalent to Mars or Moon conditions, and it is not a similarity score.

claims.limitations: Only the abstract has been read (source_access = abstract_only); class capped at B until full text is checked (gate V-10). Reference pairing is only approximate at this access level.

claims.supported_claim: Inverted stream channels at the Dakhla site, formed by differential erosion of indurated channel-fill material, are used as a terrestrial process analog for inverted fluvial channels mapped in Arabia Terra on Mars.
claims.differences: Not stated in abstract_only reading of S05; to be completed from full text.
claims.similarities: Inverted-channel morphology from differential erosion; multi-sensor remote sensing plus field/laboratory characterization of channel-fill material.
claims.not_supported: This record does not support treating Earth weather, atmospheric pressure, radiation, gravity or atmospheric composition as equivalent to Mars or Moon conditions, and it is not a similarity score.
claims.spatial_scale: Dakhla site and its mapped area per Zaki et al. 2018 Table 1 (owner-reported, not yet verified); Mars side is the Davis et al. 2019 Section 3 study extent for Arabia Terra, not a Dakhla-specific Mars feature.
claims.limitations: The pairing of Dakhla with Arabia Terra is a project decision, not stated by either source (reference_pairing_basis = project_decision_provisional). The Earth-side source is read only at abstract/highlights level, so class is capped at B. Awaiting gate V-1 (owner-reported Table 1 / Figure 13) before any geometry or state change.

claims.supported_claim: 270 MHz ground-penetrating radar surveys over small buried crater-like structures of disputed origin in the south-western Egyptian desert are used as a process analog for shallow subsurface sounding on Mars. The structures' origin is disputed; this record never calls them confirmed impact craters.
claims.differences: Not stated in the abstract of S02; the abstract reports penetration varying 'from 2 to 15 m', i.e. depth depends on local subsurface conditions. To be completed from full text.
claims.similarities: Ground-penetrating radar detection of buried structure and layered infill in an arid, radar-transparent sedimentary setting.
claims.not_supported: This record does not support treating Earth weather, atmospheric pressure, radiation, gravity or atmospheric composition as equivalent to Mars or Moon conditions, and it is not a similarity score.
claims.spatial_scale: A field of crater-like structures east of the Gilf Kebir plateau (>40,000 km^2 per S03), compared only at Mars body level (no specific reference region).
claims.limitations: S02 has now been read at abstract level (via Crossref; the publisher page blocked automated access), so the claim is class B -- never A from an abstract. S03 was read only through an automated summary and is context, not support. Orti et al. 2008 (S04) disputes the impact-origin hypothesis, not the GPR measurements. No published coordinates for the surveyed structures were found.

sources.note: 270 MHz GPR; penetration 2-15 m; compared to Martian heavily eroded mid-latitude cratered terrains.

sources.locator: automated summary of a hosted copy
sources.note: two unconfirmed origin hypotheses: hydrothermal vent complexes vs. meteorite impacts.
disputes the impact-origin hypothesis only, not the GPR measurements.

This is specific to the ARADS site, 22.4 km from the Yungay field camp; it is not an Atacama-region-wide claim (session correction 1).
claims.differences: Not stated in this reading of S08; to be completed from the remaining ~20% of the full text.
claims.similarities: Automated drilling and in-situ life-detection instrument operation in a hyperarid, low-biomass setting.
claims.not_supported: This record does not support treating Earth weather, atmospheric pressure, radiation, gravity or atmospheric composition as equivalent to Mars or Moon conditions, and it is not a similarity score.
claims.spatial_scale: The ARADS drilling field site at -24.101642, -70.138175 (point locator, as printed in S08), not the Atacama region and not Yungay.
claims.limitations: Hardening correction F-06: only approximately 80% of the open-access article was read, so S08's source_access is honestly 'partial_full_text', not 'full_text_checked' -- this claim is capped at class B, never A, until the remaining ~20% is read. This claim must never be attached to CL-ATACAMA-YUNGAY or to CL-ATACAMA as a whole.

claims.supported_claim: The 2014-2015 Holuhraun lava flow-field (fissure systems, transitional/rubbly lava morphologies, lava-water interaction, polygonal terrain) is used directly by Voigt et al. 2025 as a planetary analog for young volcanic terrains in Elysium Planitia, Mars.
claims.differences: Not stated in abstract_only reading of S07; to be completed from full text.
claims.similarities: Basaltic fissure eruption and flow-field morphology, directly compared by the source to Elysium Planitia.
claims.not_supported: This record does not support treating Earth weather, atmospheric pressure, radiation, gravity or atmospheric composition as equivalent to Mars or Moon conditions, and it is not a similarity score.
claims.spatial_scale: The 2014-2015 Holuhraun flow-field as a whole; no outline geometry exists yet (gate V-3).
claims.limitations: Only the abstract has been read (source_access = abstract_only); class capped at B until full text is checked (gate V-10). NASA GIFT Iceland 2025 is excluded as evidence for this claim (D-P2-08): it describes June 2025 work at Fagradalsfjall, Hekla and Lake Kleifarvatn, and does not mention Holuhraun.

claims.supported_claim: Ground-penetrating radar has imaged shallow layered subsurface structure both at the Gilf Kebir crater-like structures (270 MHz GPR, 2-15 m; S02) and on the floor of Jezero Crater (Perseverance's RIMFAX to 15 m, layers inclined up to 15 degrees; S25), making Gilf Kebir a candidate for evaluating GPR workflows in a dry, cratered setting.
claims.similarities: Surface GPR imaging of shallow layered structure to roughly 15 m depth in dry terrain.
claims.differences: Different instruments (270 MHz field GPR vs. RIMFAX), different materials and settings (small buried crater-like structures with disputed origin vs. the floor of a ~47.5 km impact crater), and Earth vs. Mars environment.
claims.not_supported: This record does not support treating Earth weather, atmospheric pressure, radiation, gravity or atmospheric composition as equivalent to Mars or Moon conditions, and it is not a similarity score.
claims.spatial_scale: Individual surveyed structures (Earth) vs. a rover traverse on the Jezero crater floor (Mars).
claims.limitations: The pairing with Jezero is a project decision (Project Scope §12 lists Gale / cratered Mars terrain for Gilf Kebir); neither source pairs the two sites. Earth GPR is not the same instrument as RIMFAX. The Gilf Kebir structures' origin is disputed (S04).

claims.supported_claim: Western Desert dune fields with barchan chains (S01) are a starting reference for comparing dune geometry and orientation with the barchan and linear Bagnold Dunes studied by Curiosity inside Gale Crater (S19).
claims.similarities: Wind-formed barchan dunes documented on both sides; linear dunes also studied at Bagnold.
claims.differences: Wind transport on Mars occurs in a much thinner atmosphere and under different gravity (Project Scope §12); dune dimensions are not quantified in the sources reached.
claims.not_supported: This record does not support treating Earth weather, atmospheric pressure, radiation, gravity or atmospheric composition as equivalent to Mars or Moon conditions, and it is not a similarity score.
claims.spatial_scale: The Western Desert as a region (dune-field subregion polygons still to be curated) vs. one dune field inside Gale Crater.
claims.limitations: Pairing is a project decision; El-Baz et al. (S01) compare Egyptian dunes with the north polar sand sea, not Bagnold. S01 is read at abstract level only. The whole Western Desert must not be treated as one test site.

claims.supported_claim: Inverted stream channels in the Western Desert including the Dakhla site (S05) and the ancient lake-delta system of Jezero Crater (S20) both preserve evidence of ancient flowing water, giving a broad paleohydrology context.
claims.similarities: Both preserve deposits of ancient flowing-water systems.
claims.differences: A delta and an inverted channel are different landforms (Project Scope §12); scale differs (channel ridges vs. a 45 km crater with a delta).
claims.not_supported: This record does not support treating Earth weather, atmospheric pressure, radiation, gravity or atmospheric composition as equivalent to Mars or Moon conditions, and it is not a similarity score.
claims.spatial_scale: Dakhla inverted-channel site (no verified location; oasis context point only) vs. Jezero Crater's delta.
claims.limitations: Pairing is a project decision. S05 read at abstract level only. The Dakhla burial/lithification/exhumation interpretation is tentative and site-level verification is needed (gate V-1).
